MovieScript: Inside a formal, wood-paneled courtroom, a sweating, exhausted lawyer named Saul, wearing a cheap, oversized suit, stands alone before the bench. He waves his arms passionately, looking up at the stern, elderly Judge with a pleading expression as he declares, "Oh, to be nineteen again! They did a dumb thing, but remember: nobody got hurt! Not a soul!" With a confident flourish, Saul dramatically points to a heavy CRT television sitting on a rolling cart next to him. The TV screen flickers on, loudly playing a chaotic surveillance video of blurry figures grotesquely destroying a medical dummy while a recorded voice gleefully shouts, "Stick it in the hole!" The camera focuses on a tight close-up of the Judge, who stares down at Saul with an expression of absolute, unamused disgust in the dead-silent room. The passion completely drains from Saul's face. Defeated and embarrassed, he awkwardly freezes, slowly lowers his pointing arm, and silently adjusts his cheap tie.
